data.title: A diverse array of cancer-associated MTOR mutations are hyperactivating and can predict rapamycin sensitivity
data.authors: Grabiner BC; Sabatini DM et al.

data.finding: A spectrum of cancer-associated MTOR mutations are hyperactivating and predict rapamycin sensitivity.
data.abstract_excerpt: Genes encoding components of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling axis are frequently mutated in cancer, but few mutations have been characterized in MTOR, the gene encoding the mTOR kinase. Using publicly available tumor genome sequencing data, we generated a comprehensive catalog of mTOR pathway mutations in cancer, identifying 33 MTOR mutations that confer pathway hyperactivation. The mutations cluster in six distinct regions in the C-terminal half of mTOR and occur in multiple cancer types, with one cluster particularly prominent in kidney cancer.

extracted_findings.effect: Catalogs 33 hyperactivating cancer-associated MTOR mutations (6 clusters) that can predict rapamycin sensitivity
